title: Local coexistence can remain resilient while system-level pessimism and institutional distrust weaken civic capacity
source_unit: UNDP Bosnia and Herzegovina, Social Cohesion in Bosnia and Herzegovina: Key Trends Based on SCORE BiH 2025
geography: Bosnia and Herzegovina; nationally representative and boosted locality survey coverage across all 16 regional-territorial units

denominator.unit: weighted nationally representative respondents, within an approximately 3,800-person total sample including locality boosters

observations.method: UNDP SCORE BiH 2025 face-to-face CAPI survey using stratified sampling across all 16 regional-territorial units, with weighting for entity and ethnicity and locality boosters.
observations.uncertainty: The assessment is descriptive and diagnostic; it does not establish that local cooperation causes institutional trust, or that pessimism causes disengagement or susceptibility to divisive narratives. The 2020 comparison coincided with COVID-19 and is therefore an unusual baseline.
observations.subgroup: Residents across the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska, Brčko District, ethnic and geographic groups, and boosted localities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Moderate or improving cohesion scores do not mean reconciliation is deep: low intergroup trust and lukewarm positive feelings indicate that coexistence can be functional without being emotionally close.

observations.period: 2025; system-level expectations, institutional legitimacy, and constructive citizenship

civic_duty.unit: score out of 10, up from 4.9 in 2020

observations.method: SCORE composite dimensions covering intergroup harmony, inclusive belonging, sense of progress, support for institutions, and constructive citizenship.
observations.uncertainty: Composite dimensions are context-specific measures of Bosnia and Herzegovina's social-cohesion concept and should not be treated as a universal cross-national scale without harmonization.
observations.subgroup: Citizens evaluating political stability, economic hardship, future expectations, institutions, civic knowledge, and local participation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low civic awareness alongside relatively high community cooperation may reflect weak institutional pathways and information access rather than apathy or unwillingness to contribute.

related_sources.claim: UNDP governance programming context for social cohesion, institutional trust, and civic participation.

boundary: This record captures a country-specific social-cohesion diagnostic and its local-resilience/system-pessimism pattern. It is not respondent-level raw-data ingestion, a causal model of polarization, a forecast of political stability, or proof that proposed civic-participation interventions will work.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official nine-page UNDP executive summary was reviewed, including sample design, composite dimensions, scores, 2020 comparison caveat, and policy implications.
